# Package reference

Every truck and package in the registry, generated from the `doc` section
of each package file. Trucks are collections of packages; a program loads
them with `use`. See [packages and trucks](../packages.md) for the file
format.

## The package tree

- **[pkc](pkc.md)** (truck) — pkc: the Packenger compiler, written in Packenger.
  - [pkc/util](pkc/util.md) — pkc helpers: string and vector utilities the compiler uses everywhere (prefix u_).
  - [pkc/fetch](pkc/fetch.md) — pkc: downloading packages from the registry (port of internal/registry).
  - [pkc/lock](pkc/lock.md) — pkc: lock files (port of internal/registry/lock.go).
  - [pkc/pkgfile](pkc/pkgfile.md) — pkc: package files — parse sections, patterns and emit headers (port of internal/pkgfile).
  - [pkc/lexer](pkc/lexer.md) — pkc: the tokenizer (port of internal/lang/lexer.go).
  - [pkc/lang](pkc/lang.md) — pkc: the grammar assembled from the loaded syntax packages (port of NewLang).
  - [pkc/types](pkc/types.md) — pkc: type expressions, constraints with type variables, struct layout (port of types.go).
  - [pkc/parser](pkc/parser.md) — pkc: the parser (port of internal/lang/parser.go) and the dump ast format.
  - [pkc/codegen](pkc/codegen.md) — pkc: rendering the tree through a backend truck into NASM (port of codegen.go).
  - [pkc/driver](pkc/driver.md) — pkc: the compile pipeline (port of internal/lang/driver.go).
  - [pkc/ui](pkc/ui.md) — pkc: errors and the -vb report on stderr (port of internal/ui).
  - [pkc/report](pkc/report.md) — pkc: the -vb build report (port of internal/ui's Reporter).
  - [pkc/tree](pkc/tree.md) — pkc: packenger tree — which packages built the program (port of Result.Tree).
  - [pkc/main](pkc/main.md) — pkc: the command line — the same commands, flags and messages as the Go compiler.
- **[rt](rt.md)** (truck) — The runtime truck: memory, vectors, strings, maps, files, processes, time and terminals.
  - [rt/mem](rt/mem.md) — Raw memory: an allocator on mmap, plus copy, fill, compare and pointer arithmetic.
  - [rt/vec](rt/vec.md) — Growable arrays of 64-bit words (ints, or pointers and strings with as).
  - [rt/str](rt/str.md) — Strings: slicing, searching, joining, numbers, and a string builder.
  - [rt/map](rt/map.md) — Hash map from strings to 64-bit words, iterated in insertion order.
  - [rt/io](rt/io.md) — Files and output: whole-file reads and writes, buffered stdout, stderr.
  - [rt/os](rt/os.md) — The process: environment variables, finding and running programs, exiting.
  - [rt/time](rt/time.md) — Time: a monotonic clock in nanoseconds, and durations as text.
  - [rt/term](rt/term.md) — Terminals: detecting one, and ANSI colors that respect NO_COLOR.
  - [rt/sha256](rt/sha256.md) — SHA-256: the hash that lock files pin packages with.
  - [rt/test](rt/test.md) — A tiny test library: checks that print FAIL lines, and a final PASS or FAILED.
- **[std](std.md)** (truck) — The standard language: typed, C-style statements, closed with end instead of braces.
  - [std/types](std/types.md) — The primitive types: int, u8, bool and str.
  - [std/struct](std/struct.md) — Struct declaration: struct Name ... end, one name: type field per line.
  - [std/fn](std/fn.md) — Function definition: fn name(param: type, ...) [-> type] ... end
  - [std/call](std/call.md) — Function call: name(arg, ...)
  - [std/return](std/return.md) — Return from a function; at the top level, exit with that code.
  - [std/let](std/let.md) — Declare a variable: let name [: type] = value
  - [std/assign](std/assign.md) — Assign to a variable, a field, a slice element or a dereferenced pointer.
  - [std/print](std/print.md) — Print an int, u8, bool or str, followed by a newline.
  - [std/if](std/if.md) — Conditional: if cond ... [elif cond ...]* [else ...] end
  - [std/while](std/while.md) — Loop: while cond ... [next ...] end
  - [std/do](std/do.md) — A block with its own scope: do ... end
  - [std/for](std/for.md) — Counting loop over an inclusive range: for i = a to b ... end
  - [std/exprstmt](std/exprstmt.md) — An expression used as a statement.
  - [std/true](std/true.md) — The boolean true.
  - [std/false](std/false.md) — The boolean false.
  - [std/null](std/null.md) — The null pointer: a pointer to nothing, compatible with every pointer type.
  - [std/new](std/new.md) — Allocate a struct (or any value) on the heap: new Type
  - [std/make](std/make.md) — Make a slice of n zeroed elements: make([T], n)
  - [std/len](std/len.md) — Length of a slice or a string: len(x)
  - [std/index](std/index.md) — Indexing: a[i] for slices (assignable) and s[i] for strings (a u8).
  - [std/dot](std/dot.md) — Field access through a struct pointer: p.field
  - [std/deref](std/deref.md) — Dereference a pointer: *p
  - [std/addr](std/addr.md) — Address of a place: &x
  - [std/as](std/as.md) — Convert a value to another type: x as T
  - [std/or](std/or.md) — || : logical or
  - [std/and](std/and.md) — && : logical and
  - [std/eq](std/eq.md) — == : equal
  - [std/ne](std/ne.md) — != : not equal
  - [std/lt](std/lt.md) — < : less than
  - [std/le](std/le.md) — <= : less than or equal
  - [std/gt](std/gt.md) — > : greater than
  - [std/ge](std/ge.md) — >= : greater than or equal
  - [std/add](std/add.md) — + : addition
  - [std/sub](std/sub.md) — - : subtraction
  - [std/mul](std/mul.md) — * : multiplication
  - [std/div](std/div.md) — / : integer division, rounding toward zero (like C)
  - [std/mod](std/mod.md) — % : remainder (sign follows the left operand, like C)
  - [std/not](std/not.md) — ! : logical not
  - [std/neg](std/neg.md) — - : negation
  - [std/break](std/break.md) — Leave the innermost loop: break
  - [std/continue](std/continue.md) — Skip to the next iteration of the innermost loop: continue
  - [std/global](std/global.md) — Global variable: global name: type [= value]
  - [std/const](std/const.md) — Constant: const NAME = value
  - [std/syscall](std/syscall.md) — Linux system call: syscall(number, args...) -> int
  - [std/argv](std/argv.md) — The program's command-line arguments: argv -> [str]
  - [std/cstr](std/cstr.md) — The address of a string's bytes, for system calls: cstr(s) -> ptr u8
  - [std/band](std/band.md) — & : bitwise and
  - [std/bor](std/bor.md) — | : bitwise or
  - [std/bxor](std/bxor.md) — ^ : bitwise exclusive or
  - [std/shl](std/shl.md) — << : shift left
  - [std/shr](std/shr.md) — >> : arithmetic shift right (keeps the sign)
- **[stdx](stdx.md)** (truck) — Extensions to std: compound assignment, for-in loops, match and assertions.
  - [stdx/add_assign](stdx/add_assign.md) — Compound assignment: x += y, short for x = x + y.
  - [stdx/sub_assign](stdx/sub_assign.md) — Compound assignment: x -= y, short for x = x - y.
  - [stdx/mul_assign](stdx/mul_assign.md) — Compound assignment: x *= y, short for x = x * y.
  - [stdx/div_assign](stdx/div_assign.md) — Compound assignment: x /= y, short for x = x / y.
  - [stdx/mod_assign](stdx/mod_assign.md) — Compound assignment: x %= y, short for x = x % y.
  - [stdx/forin](stdx/forin.md) — Loop over a slice or a string: for x in xs ... end
  - [stdx/match](stdx/match.md) — Choosing by value: match x, then case a, b ... else ... end
  - [stdx/assert](stdx/assert.md) — Assertion: assert cond stops the program if cond is false.
- **[bintables](bintables.md)** (truck) — Backend truck: translates Packenger packages to NASM for x86-64 Linux.
  - [bintables/add](bintables/add.md) — + : `add`.
  - [bintables/addr](bintables/addr.md) — Address of: renders the operand's addr section.
  - [bintables/alloc](bintables/alloc.md) — Helper: the heap. `__pk_alloc` returns rdi bytes of zeroed memory in rax.
  - [bintables/and](bintables/and.md) — && : short-circuit with a conditional jump; produces 0 or 1.
  - [bintables/argv](bintables/argv.md) — argv: `__pk_argv` builds a [str] from the arguments the kernel passed to the program.
  - [bintables/as](bintables/as.md) — Conversions: u8 keeps the low byte, bool tests for non-zero, others keep the bits.
  - [bintables/assign](bintables/assign.md) — Assign: store rax into a variable's slot, or through the target's address.
  - [bintables/band](bintables/band.md) — & : `and`.
  - [bintables/binop](bintables/binop.md) — Helper for binary operators: left operand in rax, right operand in rbx.
  - [bintables/bor](bintables/bor.md) — | : `or`.
  - [bintables/break](bintables/break.md) — break: jump to the end of the enclosing loop.
  - [bintables/bxor](bintables/bxor.md) — ^ : `xor`.
  - [bintables/call](bintables/call.md) — Call: push arguments right to left, call, then pop them.
  - [bintables/const](bintables/const.md) — Constant declaration: no code; the value is copied to every use.
  - [bintables/continue](bintables/continue.md) — continue: jump to the enclosing loop's next label.
  - [bintables/cstr](bintables/cstr.md) — cstr: a string's bytes start 8 bytes after its address.
  - [bintables/deref](bintables/deref.md) — Dereference: load 1 or 8 bytes from the address in rax.
  - [bintables/div](bintables/div.md) — / : signed division with `idiv` (quotient in rax).
  - [bintables/do](bintables/do.md) — do: just the block; scoping is a compile-time matter.
  - [bintables/dot](bintables/dot.md) — Field access: the struct pointer plus the field's offset; 1- or 8-byte load.
  - [bintables/eq](bintables/eq.md) — == : `cmp` and `sete`/`jne`; strings are compared by content.
  - [bintables/exprstmt](bintables/exprstmt.md) — Expression statement: compute the expression and ignore rax.
  - [bintables/false](bintables/false.md) — false: 0 in rax.
  - [bintables/fn](bintables/fn.md) — Function: label, standard stack frame, body, default return 0.
  - [bintables/ge](bintables/ge.md) — >= : `cmp`, then `setge` for a value or `jl` for a branch.
  - [bintables/global](bintables/global.md) — Global: stored in the data section as pk_g_<name>; the initializer is a store.
  - [bintables/gt](bintables/gt.md) — > : `cmp`, then `setg` for a value or `jle` for a branch.
  - [bintables/if](bintables/if.md) — Conditional: one conditional jump per condition, through each condition's jfalse.
  - [bintables/index](bintables/index.md) — Indexing with a bounds check; loads 1 or 8 bytes depending on the element type.
  - [bintables/int](bintables/int.md) — Integer literal: loads the value into rax.
  - [bintables/jfalse](bintables/jfalse.md) — Fallback branch: jump to {target} if the value in {x} is false (zero).
  - [bintables/le](bintables/le.md) — <= : `cmp`, then `setle` for a value or `jg` for a branch.
  - [bintables/len](bintables/len.md) — len: a string's length is its first qword; a slice's is at offset 8 of its header.
  - [bintables/let](bintables/let.md) — Declare: compute the value, store it in the variable's slot.
  - [bintables/lt](bintables/lt.md) — < : `cmp`, then `setl` for a value or `jge` for a branch.
  - [bintables/make](bintables/make.md) — make: allocate a slice header {data, len, cap} and n zeroed elements.
  - [bintables/mod](bintables/mod.md) — % : signed remainder with `idiv` (remainder from rdx).
  - [bintables/mul](bintables/mul.md) — * : `imul`.
  - [bintables/ne](bintables/ne.md) — != : `cmp` and `setne`/`je`; strings are compared by content.
  - [bintables/neg](bintables/neg.md) — - : `neg rax`.
  - [bintables/new](bintables/new.md) — new: allocate the type's size from the heap; rax is the pointer.
  - [bintables/not](bintables/not.md) — ! : `test` and `sete`; produces 0 or 1.
  - [bintables/null](bintables/null.md) — null: address 0 in rax.
  - [bintables/or](bintables/or.md) — || : short-circuit with a conditional jump; produces 0 or 1.
  - [bintables/panic](bintables/panic.md) — Helper: runtime errors. Prints a message to stderr and exits with status 2.
  - [bintables/print](bintables/print.md) — print: write the value and a newline to stdout with the write syscall.
  - [bintables/program](bintables/program.md) — Program skeleton: entry point, top-level code, functions, support code and data.
  - [bintables/return](bintables/return.md) — Return: value in rax (zero for a bare return), tear down the frame, ret.
  - [bintables/shl](bintables/shl.md) — << : `shl`, by a constant or by cl.
  - [bintables/shr](bintables/shr.md) — >> : `sar`, by a constant or by cl.
  - [bintables/str](bintables/str.md) — String literal: rax points at a length-prefixed byte string.
  - [bintables/streq](bintables/streq.md) — Helper: `__pk_streq` compares the strings in rax and rbx; rax is 1 if equal.
  - [bintables/storage](bintables/storage.md) — Where variables live: stack slots, parameters and globals.
  - [bintables/sub](bintables/sub.md) — - : `sub`.
  - [bintables/syscall](bintables/syscall.md) — syscall: evaluate the arguments, then load them into rax, rdi, rsi, rdx, r10, r8, r9.
  - [bintables/toolchain](bintables/toolchain.md) — How to build: assemble with nasm, link with ld.
  - [bintables/true](bintables/true.md) — true: 1 in rax.
  - [bintables/var](bintables/var.md) — Variable read: loads the variable's stack slot into rax.
  - [bintables/while](bintables/while.md) — Loop with the condition tested at the top; break and continue jump to its labels.
- **[ctables](ctables.md)** (truck) — Backend truck: translates Packenger packages to C, compiled with `cc -O2`.
  - [ctables/add](ctables/add.md) — Addition: `+` on two `int`s.
  - [ctables/addr](ctables/addr.md) — Address-of: `&x`, from the operand's `addr` section.
  - [ctables/alloc](ctables/alloc.md) — Helper: the heap. `__pk_alloc(n)` returns `n` zeroed bytes, 8-aligned.
  - [ctables/and](ctables/and.md) — Logical and: `&&`, short-circuiting.
  - [ctables/argv](ctables/argv.md) — Command-line arguments: a `[str]`, built once from `main`'s `argv`.
  - [ctables/as](ctables/as.md) — Conversion: `x as T`. To `u8` keeps the low byte, to `bool` tests for non-zero.
  - [ctables/assign](ctables/assign.md) — Assignment: to a variable, or through an address (fields, elements, `*p`).
  - [ctables/band](ctables/band.md) — Bitwise and: `&` on two `int`s.
  - [ctables/binop](ctables/binop.md) — Helper: evaluates both operands of a binary operator into temporaries.
  - [ctables/bor](ctables/bor.md) — Bitwise or: `|` on two `int`s.
  - [ctables/break](ctables/break.md) — `break`: jumps to the end of the innermost loop.
  - [ctables/bxor](ctables/bxor.md) — Bitwise xor: `^` on two `int`s.
  - [ctables/call](ctables/call.md) — Function call: the arguments are evaluated right to left, then passed.
  - [ctables/const](ctables/const.md) — Constant declaration: nothing at run time; uses are replaced by the value.
  - [ctables/continue](ctables/continue.md) — `continue`: jumps to the `next` block of the innermost loop.
  - [ctables/cstr](ctables/cstr.md) — C string: the address of a string's bytes, which end with a 0.
  - [ctables/deref](ctables/deref.md) — Dereference: `*p`, a word or (for `u8`) a byte.
  - [ctables/div](ctables/div.md) — Division: `/` on two `int`s, rounding toward zero.
  - [ctables/do](ctables/do.md) — Block: `do ... end`. Scoping is resolved by the compiler, so it is just the body.
  - [ctables/dot](ctables/dot.md) — Field access: `p.f`, at the field's offset from the struct pointer.
  - [ctables/eq](ctables/eq.md) — Equality: `==`, by value; strings by content.
  - [ctables/exprstmt](ctables/exprstmt.md) — Expression statement: evaluates the expression for its effects.
  - [ctables/false](ctables/false.md) — `false`: the word 0.
  - [ctables/fn](ctables/fn.md) — Function definition: a C function of words.
  - [ctables/ge](ctables/ge.md) — Greater than or equal: `>=` on `int`s or `u8`s, giving a `bool`.
  - [ctables/global](ctables/global.md) — Global variable: assigns the initial value, if any, where it is declared.
  - [ctables/gt](ctables/gt.md) — Greater than: `>` on `int`s or `u8`s, giving a `bool`.
  - [ctables/if](ctables/if.md) — Conditional: `if`, `elif`, `else`, with `goto`.
  - [ctables/index](ctables/index.md) — Indexing: `x[i]` on a `str` or a slice, with a bounds check.
  - [ctables/int](ctables/int.md) — Integer literal: a C `long long` constant.
  - [ctables/le](ctables/le.md) — Less than or equal: `<=` on `int`s or `u8`s, giving a `bool`.
  - [ctables/len](ctables/len.md) — Length: of a `str` (its first word) or a slice (the header's second word).
  - [ctables/let](ctables/let.md) — Variable declaration: assigns the value to the variable's storage.
  - [ctables/lt](ctables/lt.md) — Less than: `<` on `int`s or `u8`s, giving a `bool`.
  - [ctables/make](ctables/make.md) — Slice allocation: `make([T], n)`: a 24-byte header and `n` zeroed elements.
  - [ctables/mod](ctables/mod.md) — Remainder: `%` on two `int`s, with the sign of the left operand.
  - [ctables/mul](ctables/mul.md) — Multiplication: `*` on two `int`s.
  - [ctables/ne](ctables/ne.md) — Inequality: `!=`, by value; strings by content.
  - [ctables/neg](ctables/neg.md) — Negation: unary `-`. The most negative number stays as it is.
  - [ctables/new](ctables/new.md) — Allocation: `new T`, a zeroed struct from `__pk_alloc`.
  - [ctables/not](ctables/not.md) — Logical not: `!`.
  - [ctables/null](ctables/null.md) — `null`: the word 0.
  - [ctables/or](ctables/or.md) — Logical or: `||`, short-circuiting.
  - [ctables/panic](ctables/panic.md) — Helper: runtime errors. Writes the message to stderr and exits with status 2.
  - [ctables/print](ctables/print.md) — Print: writes an `int`, `u8`, `bool` or `str` and a newline to stdout.
  - [ctables/program](ctables/program.md) — Program skeleton: C headers, runtime, data, functions and `main`.
  - [ctables/return](ctables/return.md) — Return: from a function, or from the top-level code with the exit code.
  - [ctables/shl](ctables/shl.md) — Shift left: `<<`.
  - [ctables/shr](ctables/shr.md) — Arithmetic shift right: `>>`, keeping the sign.
  - [ctables/storage](ctables/storage.md) — Where variables live: a local array, C parameters and C globals.
  - [ctables/str](ctables/str.md) — String literal: a static length-prefixed byte array.
  - [ctables/streq](ctables/streq.md) — Helper: string equality, `__pk_streq(a, b)`: the lengths, then the bytes.
  - [ctables/sub](ctables/sub.md) — Subtraction: `-` on two `int`s.
  - [ctables/syscall](ctables/syscall.md) — System call: `syscall(n, args...)` with up to six arguments.
  - [ctables/toolchain](ctables/toolchain.md) — How to build: compile the C with `cc -O2`.
  - [ctables/true](ctables/true.md) — `true`: the word 1.
  - [ctables/var](ctables/var.md) — Variable read: the variable's storage.
  - [ctables/while](ctables/while.md) — Loop: `while cond ... [next ...] end`, with `goto`.
- **[webtables](webtables.md)** (truck) — Backend truck: translates Packenger packages to WebAssembly, for WASI runtimes and browsers.
  - [webtables/add](webtables/add.md) — Addition: `+`, with `i64.add`.
  - [webtables/addr](webtables/addr.md) — Address-of: `&x`, from the operand's `addr` section.
  - [webtables/alloc](webtables/alloc.md) — Helper: the heap. `$__pk_alloc(n)` returns `n` zeroed bytes, 8-aligned.
  - [webtables/and](webtables/and.md) — Logical and: `&&`, short-circuiting, with a typed `if`.
  - [webtables/argv](webtables/argv.md) — Command-line arguments: a `[str]`, built once from WASI `args_get`.
  - [webtables/as](webtables/as.md) — Conversion: `x as T`. To `u8` keeps the low byte, to `bool` tests for non-zero.
  - [webtables/assign](webtables/assign.md) — Assignment: to a variable, or through an address (fields, elements, `*p`).
  - [webtables/band](webtables/band.md) — Bitwise and: `&`, with `i64.and`.
  - [webtables/bor](webtables/bor.md) — Bitwise or: `|`, with `i64.or`.
  - [webtables/break](webtables/break.md) — `break`: leaves the innermost loop's outer block.
  - [webtables/bxor](webtables/bxor.md) — Bitwise xor: `^`, with `i64.xor`.
  - [webtables/call](webtables/call.md) — Function call: the arguments are pushed on the memory stack right to left.
  - [webtables/const](webtables/const.md) — Constant declaration: nothing at run time; uses are replaced by the value.
  - [webtables/continue](webtables/continue.md) — `continue`: leaves the body block of the innermost loop, so its `next` block runs.
  - [webtables/cstr](webtables/cstr.md) — C string: the address of a string's bytes, which end with a 0.
  - [webtables/deref](webtables/deref.md) — Dereference: `*p`, a word or (for `u8`) a byte.
  - [webtables/div](webtables/div.md) — Division: `/`, rounding toward zero, with `i64.div_s`.
  - [webtables/do](webtables/do.md) — Block: `do ... end`. Scoping is resolved by the compiler, so it is just the body.
  - [webtables/dot](webtables/dot.md) — Field access: `p.f`, a load with the field's offset as the memory offset.
  - [webtables/eq](webtables/eq.md) — Equality: `==`, by value; strings by content.
  - [webtables/exprstmt](webtables/exprstmt.md) — Expression statement: evaluates the expression and drops the value.
  - [webtables/false](webtables/false.md) — `false`: the word 0.
  - [webtables/fn](webtables/fn.md) — Function definition: a WebAssembly function of no parameters returning an `i64`.
  - [webtables/ge](webtables/ge.md) — Greater than or equal: `>=`, with `i64.ge_s`, widened to a word.
  - [webtables/global](webtables/global.md) — Global variable: stores the initial value, if any, where it is declared.
  - [webtables/gt](webtables/gt.md) — Greater than: `>`, with `i64.gt_s`, widened to a word.
  - [webtables/if](webtables/if.md) — Conditional: `if`, `elif`, `else`, as nested blocks.
  - [webtables/index](webtables/index.md) — Indexing: `x[i]` on a `str` or a slice, with a bounds check.
  - [webtables/int](webtables/int.md) — Integer literal: an `i64.const`.
  - [webtables/le](webtables/le.md) — Less than or equal: `<=`, with `i64.le_s`, widened to a word.
  - [webtables/len](webtables/len.md) — Length: of a `str` (its first word) or a slice (the header's second word).
  - [webtables/let](webtables/let.md) — Variable declaration: stores the value at the variable's address.
  - [webtables/lt](webtables/lt.md) — Less than: `<`, with `i64.lt_s`, widened to a word.
  - [webtables/make](webtables/make.md) — Slice allocation: `make([T], n)`: a 24-byte header and `n` zeroed elements.
  - [webtables/mod](webtables/mod.md) — Remainder: `%`, with the sign of the left operand, with `i64.rem_s`.
  - [webtables/mul](webtables/mul.md) — Multiplication: `*`, with `i64.mul`.
  - [webtables/ne](webtables/ne.md) — Inequality: `!=`, by value; strings by content.
  - [webtables/neg](webtables/neg.md) — Negation: unary `-`, as `0 - x`.
  - [webtables/new](webtables/new.md) — Allocation: `new T`, a zeroed struct from `$__pk_alloc`.
  - [webtables/not](webtables/not.md) — Logical not: `!`.
  - [webtables/null](webtables/null.md) — `null`: the word 0.
  - [webtables/or](webtables/or.md) — Logical or: `||`, short-circuiting, with a typed `if`.
  - [webtables/panic](webtables/panic.md) — Helper: runtime errors. Writes the message to stderr and exits with status 2.
  - [webtables/print](webtables/print.md) — Print: writes an `int`, `u8`, `bool` or `str` and a newline to stdout.
  - [webtables/program](webtables/program.md) — Program skeleton: WASI imports, memory, runtime, data, functions and `_start`.
  - [webtables/return](webtables/return.md) — Return: restores the stack pointer, then returns the value.
  - [webtables/shl](webtables/shl.md) — Shift left: `<<`, the count taken modulo 64, with `i64.shl`.
  - [webtables/shr](webtables/shr.md) — Arithmetic shift right: `>>`, the count taken modulo 64, with `i64.shr_s`.
  - [webtables/storage](webtables/storage.md) — Where variables live: a stack in linear memory, and a globals area.
  - [webtables/str](webtables/str.md) — String literal: a passive data segment, copied to the heap on first use.
  - [webtables/streq](webtables/streq.md) — Helper: string equality, `$__pk_streq(a, b)`: the lengths, then the bytes.
  - [webtables/sub](webtables/sub.md) — Subtraction: `-`, with `i64.sub`.
  - [webtables/syscall](webtables/syscall.md) — System call: Linux syscall numbers, translated to WASI.
  - [webtables/toolchain](webtables/toolchain.md) — How to build and run: `wat2wasm`, then a WASI runtime.
  - [webtables/true](webtables/true.md) — `true`: the word 1.
  - [webtables/var](webtables/var.md) — Variable read: a word loaded from the variable's address in linear memory.
  - [webtables/wasi](webtables/wasi.md) — Helper: the WASI runtime: Linux syscalls translated to WASI calls.
  - [webtables/while](webtables/while.md) — Loop: `while cond ... [next ...] end`, as a `loop` inside a `block`.
